content: CHL1, also referred to as the close homolog of L1 (CHL1), is a protein in humans encoded by the CHL1 gene. This protein belongs to the family of cell adhesion molecules and is closely related to the L1 protein. In melanocytic cells, the expression of the CHL1 gene may be regulated by the microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF). Additionally, CHL1 can function as a helicase protein during the interphase stage of mitosis, playing a role in DNA unwinding and replication processes. The CHL1 protein exhibits dynamic localization within the cell, indicating that it not only performs multiple distinct functions but also operates in various cellular compartments. This versatility underscores its importance in cellular processes and its potential involvement in diverse biological roles.
